name: Russell Brand
role: Comedian, actor and podcaster; political commentator on Rumble
summary: Brand's politics have changed over time. In 2013-2015 he rejected voting, criticised capitalism and called for a non-violent revolution, then in 2015 urged people to vote Labour. From about 2021 he has presented himself as anti-establishment, critical of government, big business and public-health policy, and since 2024 has described himself as a Christian. Most of his recorded political statements are general critiques, so few of the specific statements can be answered.

corporate-influence.rationale: Says the political system 'administrates for large corporations' and politicians service only corporate needs.

decide-locally.rationale: Calls for 'radical decentralization, radical federalization' and for communities and states built from the bottom up rather than imposed from the top.

direct-action.rationale: In 2013-14 told people to stop voting and said only creative direct action will move corporations; Wikipedia reports he dropped the no-voting line in 2015, so not rated higher.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Says present government measures on climate change are indifferent and will not solve it, and that capitalism will not change without direct action.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale is about other international bodies (such as the EU, WTO, IMF or WHO) or about support, funding or reform without enforcement powers, and the statement now asks whether the UN should have powers to enforce its decisions against member states.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Names a 'socialist egalitarian system' as what he wants; he does not say outcomes should be equal in so many words.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Wants drug addiction 'decriminalized and regulated, not left in the hands of criminals'; he is speaking of addiction and stops short of recreational use generally.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: Hopes to see donations and lobbying removed from politics entirely, saying politics has been captured by the donor and lobbyist class.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Says the Thames water utility should be owned and run by the community who live there, not as a for-profit entity.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: In a March 2022 clip he said the mainstream media, culture and government are 'not your friend' and that powerful groups operate together to create systems that benefit them and disadvantage others (London Economic, 2023). He did not use the word 'pacify' or say these institutions reproduce the social order.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Describes the political class's 'lies, treachery, deceit' and says politicians are only interested in servicing corporations.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Mocks US spending of $5bn 'promoting democracy' in Ukraine and says to do it in its own country.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Criticises a culture that worships rationalism and materialism and has made faith in God central to his life since his 2024 baptism.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Wants heavy taxation of corporations and 'massive responsibility' imposed on energy companies exploiting the environment.

state-harmful.rationale: Says there needs to be a centralised administrative system and a government, though he would call it something else.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Calls for a socialist egalitarian system built on massive redistribution of wealth and heavy taxation of corporations (Newsnight).

notes: Views changed over time. 2013-2014: refused to vote, called for a non-violent revolution and for wealth redistribution. April 2015: urged people to vote Labour and backed Corbyn, which the 2014 answers do not reflect. 2021 onward: anti-establishment commentary on COVID-19 measures, the WHO treaty and government. 2024: baptised as a Christian and endorsed Robert F. Kennedy Jr. (Wikipedia; the endorsement is not used in any answer, as it was only reported in summary). The 2013 and 2014 statements are taken from a secondary summary (Wikipedia) and a 2014 interview, not from full transcripts, and no full transcript of his recent podcast or Rumble shows was available to read. Legal allegations against him are not political positions and are not used. Early-exit rule not applied: he has documented political statements. Inclusion is not expected to pass with this few answers. Later pass (claude-sonnet-5-5, 2026-11-19): added the 2013 Newsnight interview, the Democracy Now! transcript and two 2022-23 Trews videos (Ukraine, Covid data) and the 2024 Tucker Carlson Show transcript; searched themes: economy, government, drugs, climate, foreign policy, surveillance. YouTube rate-limited further caption searches.
